item.title: The 7 Best WordPress Plugins for Site Security in 2025
item.dc:creator: Gareth Cross
item.content:encoded:
Keeping your WordPress site secure is an absolute must for any website owner. With new threats emerging all the time, the right plugins can protect you from hackers, malware, brute force attacks, and more. Here are the top 7 security plugins you should consider for your site in 2025:

  1. Wordfence Security

Why it's great: Wordfence offers a comprehensive firewall, malware scanner, and live traffic monitoring. Its free version is quite powerful, and the premium plan unlocks additional features such as country blocking and advanced malware analysis.

Recommended for: All site owners, from beginners to experts.

  1. Sucuri Security

Why it's great: Sucuri provides DNS-level firewall protection, malware scanning, monitoring, and backup integration. If your site gets hacked, Sucuri's team can clean it up for you.

Recommended for: Those wanting enterprise-grade protection and peace of mind.

  1. Solid Security (formerly iThemes Security)

Why it's great: Offers robust features like two-factor authentication, brute force protection, file change detection, and activity logging. A great plugin for hardening WordPress.

Recommended for: Users needing an easy setup process with powerful, customizable options.

  1. All-In-One Security (AIOS)

Why it's great: Provides strong site hardening, login lockdowns, security scanning, and firewall features. Its free version is excellent for basic security needs.

Recommended for: Users who want maximum security for free.

  1. Jetpack Security

Why it's great: Bundles malware scanning, daily backups, brute force protection, and real-time activity logging. It offers a wide range of additional features beyond security.

Recommended for: Bloggers and site owners looking for an all-in-one solution.

  1. MalCare

Why it's great: MalCare is known for its deep malware scanning and one-click malware removal, all without impacting site speed. It also offers emergency cleanup services and firewall protection.

Recommended for: Anyone wanting fast, hassle-free malware removal.

  1. Defender Security

Why it's great: This plugin stands out for its user-friendly interface, malware scans, firewall rules, login protection, and IP blocking. It's great for beginners seeking a non-technical security solution.

Recommended for: Site owners who want reliable security with simple setup and management.

Final Thoughts

No single plugin will secure your site against every possible threat. For best results, combine one or more of these plugins and keep your site, plugins, and themes updated. Regular backups and monitoring are also critical for keeping your WordPress site safe.

Which security plugin do you rely on? Share your experience in the comments!

item.title: The Top 12 Sources of Digital Media Buying in the UK (2025): A Comprehensive Guide for UK buyers
item.dc:creator: Gareth Cross
item.content:encoded:
The UK digital advertising market is thriving, with the social media advertising sector alone projected to reach £9.95 billion in 2025. For British marketers and businesses, understanding where to allocate media buying budgets across this increasingly complex landscape has never been more crucial.

Digital channels now dominate UK advertising spend,3. TikTok Adsads.tiktok.com with online platforms accounting for a growing majority of total ad investment. In this comprehensive guide, we'll explore the top 12 sources of digital media buying specifically for the UK market in 2025, complete with data-backed insights, UK audience demographics, purchasing methods, and the key trend shifts that are reshaping how British brands connect with consumers.

1. Google Ads (Search & Display)

Platform URL: https://ads.google.com

UK Market Position: Google commands approximately 90% of UK search traffic, making it the dominant platform for intent-driven advertising. Google UK's advertising ecosystem includes Search, Display Network, Shopping, and YouTube.

UK Audience Reach: Reaches virtually all UK internet users across multiple touchpoints - search queries, Gmail, YouTube, and millions of UK websites in the Display Network. Particularly strong for reaching consumers atthe moment of purchase intent - from "plumbers near me" to "best laptops UK 2025."

Who Can You Reach: UK consumers actively searching for products/services, B2B decision-makers, local customers across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland. Demographic targeting includes age, location, household income, and detailed interest-based segments.

How to Buy: Self-service through Google Ads platform using GBP budgets. Options include CPC (cost-per-click), CPM (cost-per-thousand impressions), and CPA (cost-per-acquisition) bidding. AI-powered Smart Bidding optimises campaigns automatically. UK businesses can work with Google Partner agencies for managed services.

UK Trend Shifts: Growing dominance of mobile search (over 65% of UK searches), voice search optimization for UK accents, and increased investment in Google Shopping for e-commerce retailers post-Brexit.2. Meta Ads (Facebook & Instagram)

2. Meta Ads (Facebook & Instagram)

Platform URL: https://business.facebook.com

UK Market Position: The UK social media advertising market is projected to reach £9.95 billion in 2025, with Meta platforms dominating. Facebook and Instagram combined represent the largest social advertising opportunity for UK brands.

UK Audience Reach: Facebook: 44.84 million UK users (approximately 67% of the population). Instagram: 31.6 million UK users, with particularly strong engagement among 18-34 year olds. Collectively reaches 93% of UK social media users.

Who Can You Reach: UK consumers across all age groups (Facebook skews 35+, Instagram 18-34), lifestyle interests, purchasing behaviours. Exceptional for UK B2C brands, e-commerce, local businesses from Cornwall to the Highlands, and increasingly B2B through professional targeting. Strong reach in major UK cities: London, Manchester, Birmingham, Glasgow, Leeds.

How to Buy: Self-service through Meta Ads Manager with auction-based GBP bidding. CPC, CPM, and CPA options. AI-powered Advantage+ campaigns optimise across Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, and Audience Network. 83% of UK mobile social ad spending projected through mobile by 2029.

UK Trend Shifts: Decline in organic reach (now under 5% for business pages) making paid advertising essential. Instagram Reels overtaking feed posts for UK engagement. Growing use of WhatsApp Business API for UK customer service integration. Post-COVID surge in Facebook Marketplace advertising for local UK businesses.3. TikTok Ads

Platform URL: https://ads.tiktok.com

UK Market Position: TikTok's UK ad revenue is growing 24.5% year-on-year, making it one of the fastest-growing platforms for British advertisers. Projected global ad revenue of $32.4 billion in 2025, with strong UK contribution.

UK Audience Reach: Over 23 million UK users, with 69% aged 18-34. TikTok reaches 34% of the UK population and commands exceptional engagement rates - UK users spend an average 52 minutes per day on the platform.

Who Can You Reach: Predominantly Gen Z and Millennials in the UK, though older demographics are growing rapidly. Perfect for UK fashion brands, beauty products, entertainment, food & beverage, and increasingly financial services targeting younger UK consumers. Strong performance for brands in trendy UK cities and university towns.

How to Buy: Self-service through TikTok Ads Manager with GBP budgeting. Options include In-Feed Ads, TopView, Branded Hashtag Challenges, and Branded Effects. CPC, CPM, and CPV (cost-per-view) models. TikTok's Creative Centre provides UK-specific insights and trends.

UK Trend Shifts: 81% of UK marketers plan to increase TikTok investment in 2025 - highest of any platform. TikTok Shop integration driving social commerce growth in the UK. Brands seeing 2.4x direct ROAS, and 4.2x when factoring in Amazon UK sales influence. UK creators commanding premium rates for brand partnerships.4. LinkedIn Ads

Platform URL: https://business.linkedin.com/marketing-solutions

UK Market Position: LinkedIn's global ad revenue is forecast to reach $8.2 billion in 2025 (18.3% YoY growth), with the UK being one of its strongest markets. LinkedIn reaches 91.4% of the eligible UK B2B advertising audience.

UK Audience Reach: Over 33 million UK professionals on LinkedIn - that's approximately 49% of the UK population. Particularly strong in London (8+ million users), Manchester, Birmingham, and Edinburgh financial districts. UK users include C-suite executives, managers, and decision-makers across all industries.

Who Can You Reach: UK B2B decision-makers, professionals by job title (Marketing Directors, IT Managers, CEOs), company size, industry sector, seniority level. Perfect for reaching UK financial services, technology, professional services, education, and industrial sectors. Users have 2x the buying power of average UK web audiences.

How to Buy: Self-service through LinkedIn Campaign Manager with GBP budgets. CPC and CPM bidding, with typical UK CPCs of £5-£8. Sponsored Content, Message Ads, Dynamic Ads, and Text Ads available. Lead Gen Forms achieve 10% conversion rates. 82% of UK B2B marketers use LinkedIn Ads.

UK Trend Shifts: LinkedIn conversion rates 2x higher than other platforms for UK B2B. Video content seeing 50% higher engagement. LinkedIn Live events popular for UK thought leadership. Growing adoption of LinkedIn Learning integration for recruitment marketing. Brexit has increased focus on UK-specific professional targeting rather than pan-European campaigns.5. Amazon Advertising

Platform URL: https://advertising.amazon.co.uk

UK Market Position: Amazon UK advertising is experiencing explosive 24% YoY growth, with UK ad revenue contributing significantly to Amazon's projected global $60.6 billion retail media ad revenue in 2025.

UK Audience Reach: Over 30 million monthly active UK shoppers on Amazon.co.uk. 89% of UK online shoppers use Amazon, with Prime members spending significantly more. Reaches consumers at the critical point of purchase intent.

Who Can You Reach: UK consumers actively shopping across all product categories. Particularly effective for e-commerce brands, consumer goods manufacturers, and retailers. Demographics skew towards AB/C1 households with disposable income. Strong reach across all UK regions, from urban centres to rural areas.

How to Buy: Self-service through Amazon Advertising Console with GBP budgets. Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands, Sponsored Display, and Amazon DSP available. CPC bidding model with typical UK costs of £0.50-£2.00 per click depending on category. Performance-driven with direct attribution to sales.

UK Trend Shifts: Amazon UK becoming essential for product discovery - 54% of UK consumers start product searches on Amazon rather than Google. Integration with Amazon Prime Video ads offering new brand awareness opportunities. Amazon Live shopping events gaining traction in UK. Post-pandemic surge in UK grocery and household goods advertising on platform.6. YouTube Advertising

Platform URL: https://ads.youtube.com

UK Market Position: YouTube is the UK's second-largest search engine and part of Google's ecosystem. Digital video ad spend in the UK surged 18% YoY to reach significant market share, with YouTube dominating.

UK Audience Reach: Over 47 million UK users watch YouTube monthly - that's 70% of the UK population. UK viewers watch over 1 billion hours of YouTube daily. Strong across all age groups but particularly 16-44 demographics.

Who Can You Reach: Mass UK audience across all demographics, interests, and locations. Exceptional for brand awareness campaigns, product launches, tutorials, and entertainment content. Reaches cord-cutters who've abandoned traditional UK TV. Strong performance for UK automotive, technology, beauty, gaming, and education sectors.

How to Buy: Through Google Ads platform with GBP budgets. TrueView In-Stream (skippable), Non-skippable ads, Bumper ads, and YouTube Shorts ads available. CPV (cost-per-view) and CPM bidding. UK advertisers only pay when viewers watch 30 seconds or interact.

UK Trend Shifts: YouTube Shorts experiencing explosive growth in UK, competing with TikTok. CTV (Connected TV) viewing growing as UK households cut traditional TV subscriptions - over 60% of UK YouTube watch time now on TV screens. AI-powered targeting improving UK campaign performance. Integration with Google's broader ecosystem providing better attribution.7. Programmatic Display (The Trade Desk & Google DV360)

Platform URLs: https://www.thetradedesk.com / https://marketingplatform.google.com/about/display-video-360/

UK Market Position: Programmatic advertising now accounts for over 90% of UK digital display ad spend. The UK programmatic market is highly sophisticated, with London serving as a European programmatic hub.

UK Audience Reach: Access to virtually all UK internet users across thousands of UK publisher websites, apps, Connected TV platforms, and digital-out-of-home (DOOH) inventory. Reaches audiences across premium UK news sites (Telegraph, Guardian, Times), entertainment, and specialist publishers.

Who Can You Reach: Highly targeted UK audiences based on demographics, interests, behaviours, location data, and first-party data matching. Perfect for UK brand awareness campaigns, retargeting, and omnichannel strategies. Access to UK-specific audience segments and contextual targeting.

How to Buy: Through demand-side platforms (DSPs) with GBP budgets. Typically requires minimum spend commitments and agency/trading desk partnerships for The Trade Desk. Google DV360 accessible through Google Marketing Platform. Real-time bidding (RTB) with CPM pricing. Advanced options include private marketplace (PMP) deals with premium UK publishers.

UK Trend Shifts: 83% of UK senior marketers using AI for programmatic optimization. Growth of UK retail media networks providing first-party data for programmatic targeting. DOOH programmatic growing rapidly across UK high streets and transit networks. Privacy-first solutions with clean rooms replacing third-party cookies. Supply-path optimization reducing ad fraud in UK market.8. X (formerly Twitter) Ads

Platform URL: https://ads.twitter.com

UK Market Position: X maintains strong presence in UK news, politics, and real-time conversations. Platform particularly influential among UK journalists, politicians, and thought leaders.

UK Audience Reach: Approximately 19.05 million UK users. Strong engagement during live UK events: sports (Premier League, cricket), politics (elections, PM speeches), entertainment (TV shows, awards). Reaches affluent, educated UK demographics.

Who Can You Reach: UK news enthusiasts, B2B professionals, tech-savvy consumers, sports fans, and politically engaged audiences. Particularly effective during major UK events and cultural moments. Strong reach in London, Manchester, Edinburgh.

How to Buy: Self-service through X Ads Manager with GBP budgets. Promoted Tweets, Promoted Accounts, and Promoted Trends available. CPC, CPM, and CPE (cost-per-engagement) bidding. Trend takeovers command premium pricing for UK visibility.

UK Trend Shifts: Platform volatility under new ownership affecting UK advertiser confidence. However, real-time marketing opportunities remain valuable for UK brands during live events. X Premium (subscription) changing content dynamics. Video content gaining traction in UK market.9. Snapchat Ads

Platform URL: https://ads.snapchat.com

UK Market Position: Snapchat's projected global ad revenue of $6 billion in 2025 includes significant UK contribution. Platform particularly strong among younger UK demographics.

UK Audience Reach: Over 20 million UK users, with 75% aged 13-34. Reaches 30% of the UK population. Exceptional engagement - UK users open app an average of 30+ times daily.

Who Can You Reach: Gen Z and younger Millennials in the UK. Perfect for UK fashion, beauty, entertainment, food & beverage brands targeting younger consumers. Strong in university cities and among UK students.

How to Buy: Self-service through Snapchat Ads Manager with GBP budgets. Snap Ads, Story Ads, Collection Ads, and AR Lenses available. CPC, CPM, and swipe-up bidding models. UK-specific AR filters popular for branded campaigns.

UK Trend Shifts: Snapchat+ subscription tier growing in UK. AR shopping experiences gaining traction among UK fashion brands. Spotlight (TikTok competitor) growing UK user engagement. Integration with UK retailers for social commerce.10. Pinterest Ads

Platform URL: https://ads.pinterest.com

UK Market Position: Pinterest's global ad revenue projected at $4.2 billion in 2025. Platform particularly effective for UK lifestyle and visual discovery marketing.

UK Audience Reach: Over 13 million UK monthly active users, with 60% female, 40% male. Strong among UK homeowners, wedding planners, DIY enthusiasts, and lifestyle shoppers. Average UK household income of Pinterest users higher than other platforms.

Who Can You Reach: UK consumers in planning mode - home renovation, weddings, fashion, recipes, travel. Exceptional for UK retail, home & garden, fashion, food & beverage, and lifestyle brands. Pinterest users are intentional shoppers with 85% making purchases based on pins.

How to Buy: Self-service through Pinterest Ads Manager with GBP budgets. Promoted Pins, Shopping Ads, Carousel Ads, and Video Pins available. CPC and CPM bidding. Pinterest Lens (visual search) offers unique UK product discovery opportunities.

UK Trend Shifts: Pinterest users 7x more likely to say platform is most influential in purchase decisions versus other social platforms. Video pins seeing 2x engagement in UK. Growing male audience changing platform demographics. UK seasonal campaigns (Christmas, Mother's Day) performing exceptionally well.11. Reddit Ads

Platform URL: https://ads.reddit.com

UK Market Position: Reddit's global ad revenue projected at $2.2 billion in 2025. Growing platform for UK community-based and authentic marketing.

UK Audience Reach: Over 22 million UK monthly visitors. Strong among tech-savvy, educated UK users. Particularly powerful for niche UK communities - from r/UnitedKingdom to r/LondonSocialClub to specific interest subreddits.

Who Can You Reach: UK tech enthusiasts, gamers, hobbyists, and passionate community members. Perfect for UK tech products, gaming, finance (r/UKPersonalFinance), automotive, and entertainment. Audience appreciates authentic, non-salesy content.

How to Buy: Self-service through Reddit Ads platform with GBP budgets. Promoted Posts appear in UK subreddit feeds. CPC and CPM bidding. Takeover ads available for maximum UK visibility. Community-first approach essential for success.

UK Trend Shifts: Reddit IPO bringing more sophisticated UK advertising tools. Community advertising becoming more mainstream for UK brands. AMA (Ask Me Anything) format popular for UK brand engagement. UK financial services finding strong ROI through targeted subreddit advertising.12. Spotify Advertising

Platform URL: https://ads.spotify.com

UK Market Position: Digital audio advertising experiencing significant growth as UK consumers embrace streaming. Spotify dominates UK music streaming market.

UK Audience Reach: Over 19 million UK Spotify users. Strong across all age groups but particularly 18-44. UK free tier users (ad-supported) represent substantial reach for advertisers. Engaged audience spending average 2.5+ hours daily listening.

Who Can You Reach: UK music lovers, podcast enthusiasts, commuters, gym-goers, and workers. Demographic, interest, and contextual targeting available. Perfect for UK automotive brands (in-car listening), fitness, entertainment, consumer goods. Audio advertising reaches users during intimate moments - commuting, exercising, working from home.

How to Buy: Through Spotify Ad Studio (self-service) or Spotify Advertising sales team for larger UK campaigns. Audio ads, video takeovers, and sponsored playlists available. CPM bidding with GBP budgets. Minimum spends apply for certain formats.

UK Trend Shifts: Podcast advertising exploding in UK - revenue growing 20%+ YoY. UK commuters returning to offices post-pandemic increasing weekday listening. Spotify Wrapped campaigns providing annual UK cultural moments for brand integration. Audio-first creativity becoming essential for UK marketers.Key UK Digital Media Buying Trends for 2025

As we've explored these 12 major platforms, several overarching trends are reshaping the UK digital advertising landscape:

1. Mobile-First Dominance: 83% of UK social media ad spending will flow through mobile by 2029. All UK campaigns must prioritize mobile-optimized creative and experiences.

2. Decline of Organic Reach: Organic reach on social platforms has plummeted to under 5% for UK business pages, making paid advertising essential rather than optional for British brands.

3. AI-Powered Optimization: 83% of UK senior marketers now use AI for campaign optimization, with platforms offering increasingly sophisticated automation for bidding, targeting, and creative testing.

4. Privacy-First Targeting: With third-party cookies phasing out, UK advertisers are pivoting to first-party data strategies, clean rooms, and contextual targeting to reach audiences while respecting privacy.

5. Video & Short-Form Content: UK consumers are gravitating toward video content, with YouTube Shorts, TikTok, Instagram Reels, and Snapchat Spotlight driving engagement. UK brands must adapt creative strategies accordingly.

6. Connected TV Growth: Over 60% of UK YouTube watch time now occurs on TV screens, and streaming platforms are offering new CTV advertising opportunities as British households continue cutting traditional TV subscriptions.

7. Social Commerce Integration: From TikTok Shop to Instagram Shopping, UK consumers are increasingly comfortable purchasing directly within social platforms, blurring the line between discovery and transaction.

8. Audio & Podcast Advertising: UK podcast advertising revenue is growing 20%+ YoY as British consumers embrace audio content during commutes, exercise, and work-from-home routines.

Conclusion: Building Your UK Media Mix

For UK marketers in 2025, success lies not in choosing a single platform but in strategically combining multiple channels to reach your audience throughout their customer journey:

  • Upper Funnel (Awareness): YouTube, TikTok, Programmatic Display, Spotify
  • Mid Funnel (Consideration): Meta, LinkedIn, Pinterest, X
  • Lower Funnel (Conversion): Google Ads, Amazon Advertising
  • Retention & Loyalty: Meta remarketing, Email (integrated with social)

The UK digital advertising market's projected growth to £9.95 billion in social alone demonstrates the immense opportunity for British businesses. By understanding each platform's unique strengths, UK audience characteristics, and trend shifts, you can build a media buying strategy that delivers measurable results for your UK campaigns.

The key is to test, measure, and optimize continuously - using the data-driven insights available across these platforms to refine your approach and maximize ROI in the competitive UK market.

Ready to elevate your UK digital advertising strategy? Contact GLC Web Solutions for expert media buying guidance tailored to the British market.

item.title: Google's December 2025 Core Update: What You Need to Know
item.dc:creator: Gareth Cross
item.content:encoded:
Google has rolled out another significant algorithm update in December 2025, and website owners across the globe are already seeing the impact on their search rankings. Understanding what has changed and how to respond is crucial for maintaining and improving your site's visibility in search results.

What's Changed in the December 2025 Core Update?

This latest core update continues Google's ongoing mission to reward high-quality, user-focused content whilst demoting sites that rely on manipulative SEO tactics. According to early analysis from the SEO community, this update places even greater emphasis on:

Content Quality and Depth: Google is now better at identifying thin, superficial content that doesn't genuinely answer user queries. Sites with comprehensive, well-researched content are seeing positive movements.

User Experience Signals: Page experience metrics continue to play a vital role. Sites with poor Core Web Vitals, intrusive interstitials, or confusing navigation structures are being penalised more heavily.

E-E-A-T Principles: Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, and Trustworthiness remain central to Google's ranking algorithm. Sites demonstrating genuine expertise and providing author credentials are performing better.

Helpful Content: The update builds upon previous helpful content updates, further rewarding content written primarily for users rather than search engines.

How to Monitor the Impact on Your Website

If you want to understand how the December update has affected your site, here are the key steps to take:

  1. Check Google Search Console

Log into your Google Search Console account and review your performance data. Look for significant changes in:

  • Impressions and clicks from organic search
  • Average position for your key queries
  • Click-through rates (CTR)

Compare data from the last 28 days against the previous period to spot any notable trends.

  1. Monitor Your Rankings

Use rank tracking tools like SEMrush, Ahrefs, or Moz to monitor your positions for target keywords. Pay particular attention to:

  • Pages that have dropped significantly in rankings
  • Queries where you've lost visibility
  • Competitors who may have gained positions you previously held
  1. Analyse Your Traffic in Google Analytics

Review your organic traffic patterns in Google Analytics 4. Look for:

  • Sudden drops or increases in organic sessions
  • Changes in user behaviour metrics (bounce rate, time on page, pages per session)
  • Shifts in which pages are receiving the most organic traffic
  1. Review Your Core Web Vitals

Check your Core Web Vitals scores in Google Search Console. Poor performance in Largest Contentful Paint (LCP), First Input Delay (FID), or Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) could be contributing to ranking losses.

  1. Conduct a Content Audit

Evaluate your content against Google's quality guidelines:

  • Is it genuinely helpful to your audience?
  • Does it demonstrate expertise and authority?
  • Is it written primarily for users or search engines?
  • Does it provide unique value that can't be found elsewhere?

Recovering From a Negative Impact

If you've been negatively affected by the update, don't panic. Recovery is possible, but it requires strategic action:

  • Improve content quality by adding depth, research, and expert insights
  • Enhance user experience by improving site speed and navigation
  • Remove or improve thin, low-quality content
  • Build genuine authority through quality backlinks and author credentials
  • Focus on creating content that genuinely serves user needs

Need Expert SEO Guidance?

Navigating Google's algorithm updates can be challenging, especially when your business depends on organic search visibility. At GLC Web Solutions, we specialise in helping businesses understand and respond to Google's ever-changing search landscape. Our SEO consultancy services include comprehensive site audits, technical SEO improvements, content strategy development, and ongoing monitoring to ensure your website maintains strong search performance.

Whether you've been impacted by the December update or you want to proactively strengthen your site's SEO foundation, we're here to help. Get in touch with us through our contact form to discuss how we can support your SEO goals and help your website achieve the visibility it deserves.

item.title: AI Browsers in 2025: Comprehensive Review of Comet, Atlas, Dia, and Claude for Chrome
item.dc:creator: Gareth Cross
item.content:encoded:
The web browsing landscape is undergoing a dramatic transformation in 2025, with artificial intelligence taking center stage. As AI becomes deeply integrated into our daily digital lives, a new generation of browsers and browser extensions has emerged, promising to revolutionize how we interact with the web. In this comprehensive review, we'll examine four leading AI-powered browsing solutions: Comet, Atlas, Dia, and Claude for Chrome.

Comet by Perplexity AI

Release Date: July 9, 2025 (Limited release), October 2, 2025 (Global free release)

Pricing: Free (Previously $200/month for Perplexity Max subscribers during beta)

Platform Availability: Windows, macOS (July 2025), Android (November 20, 2025), iOS coming soon

Comet represents Perplexity AI's ambitious entry into the browser market. Built on Chromium, Comet uses Perplexity as its default search engine and integrates AI capabilities directly into the browsing experience.

Key Features:

AI-powered sidebar that can summarize text, answer questions, and take actions

Seamless integration with Perplexity's answer engine

Tab organization and management

Email drafting assistance

Shopping and product research capabilities

Multi-step task automation

What Makes It Stand Out:

Comet's biggest advantage is its zero-cost model. After launching as an expensive premium feature, Perplexity made the strategic decision to offer Comet completely free to everyone. This democratizes access to AI-powered browsing at a time when competitors are charging premium prices.

The browser excels at research-focused tasks, leveraging Perplexity's strength in providing cited, accurate answers from across the web. For users who value fact-checking and sourced information, Comet provides an excellent browsing companion.

Limitations:

As a relatively new browser, Comet is still developing its extension ecosystem

Heavy reliance on Perplexity's AI means users are tied to one AI provider

Privacy considerations around data collection for advertising (Perplexity has been open about its interest in targeted ads)

ChatGPT Atlas by OpenAI

Release Date: October 21, 2025

Pricing: Free tier available, Agent Mode requires ChatGPT Plus ($20/month), Pro, or Business subscription

Platform Availability: macOS (October 2025), Windows, iOS, and Android coming soon

OpenAI's Atlas browser represents the company's vision of an AI-native browsing experience, where ChatGPT is embedded directly into every web page rather than being an add-on feature.

Key Features:

Always-available ChatGPT sidebar on every webpage

Article and document summarization

Page content analysis and extraction

Agent Mode for autonomous task completion

Context retention across tabs

Automated form filling and multi-step processes

What Makes It Stand Out:

Atlas's Agent Mode is revolutionary. It can autonomously browse websites, book flights, complete research across multiple sites, and handle complex workflows while you continue with other tasks. This represents a significant leap toward truly agentic AI that can work independently.

With 800 million weekly ChatGPT users, Atlas has immediate access to a massive potential user base already familiar with OpenAI's AI assistant. The integration is seamless for existing ChatGPT users.

Limitations:

Currently Mac-only, limiting business adoption

Most powerful features locked behind paid subscription

Still developing enterprise security and management features

Raised concerns about changes to search behavior and traffic patterns for websites

Dia by The Browser Company

Release Date: June 2025 (Beta launch)

Pricing: Free tier available, Dia Pro $20/month for unlimited AI features

Platform Availability: macOS, Windows, with broader platform support expected

The Browser Company, creators of the innovative Arc browser, launched Dia as their next-generation AI-first browser experience. Dia takes a different approach by redesigning the browser interface around AI rather than retrofitting AI into a traditional browser.

Key Features:

AI-first URL bar for navigation, search, and prompts

Tab-aware chatbot that understands context across open tabs

Customizable "Skills" for personalized workflows

Content creation in your writing style

Automated shopping and task completion

Privacy-focused design

What Makes It Stand Out:

Dia's interface innovation sets it apart. The URL bar functions as a universal input that intelligently routes requests to navigation, search, or AI assistance. This streamlined approach reduces context switching and makes AI feel more natural.

The customizable Skills feature allows users to teach Dia specific workflows and preferences, making it more personalized over time. CEO Josh Miller has indicated plans for multiple subscription tiers ranging from $5 to hundreds of dollars monthly, suggesting enterprise-focused features are coming.

Limitations:

Free tier users face usage limits on AI features (exact limits not specified)

Still in beta with some reliability issues reported

Smaller user base compared to established browsers

Broad data access behind SSO raises privacy concerns

Claude for Chrome by Anthropic

Release Date: December 2025 (Expanded availability)

Pricing: Requires Claude subscription - Pro ($20/month or $200/year), Max ($200/month), Team ($25-30/month per person), or Enterprise

Platform Availability: Chrome browser extension (works on any platform running Chrome)

Unlike the standalone browsers above, Claude for Chrome is an extension that brings Anthropic's Claude AI assistant directly into your Chrome browsing experience.

Key Features:

Full webpage analysis and interaction

Automated navigation, clicking, and form filling

Multi-step workflow automation

Workflow recording to "teach" Claude custom tasks

Integration with Claude Code for development workflows

Background task execution

Scheduled workflow automation

What Makes It Stand Out:

Claude for Chrome's workflow training feature is particularly impressive. You can record yourself completing a task once, and Claude learns to replicate it autonomously. This makes it exceptional for repetitive tasks like expense reports, CRM updates, or email management.

The extension works within your existing Chrome setup, meaning you don't need to switch browsers or lose your current extensions, bookmarks, and settings. This significantly lowers the barrier to adoption.

Integration with Claude Code makes it powerful for developers who can connect testing and iteration workflows directly to their browser.

Limitations:

Requires a paid Claude subscription (no free tier for the extension)

Only works in Chrome (not available for other browsers)

Deep access to browsing activity raises privacy considerations

You're trusting Claude to act as your representative without oversight

Comparative Analysis

Best for Budget-Conscious Users: Comet wins here with its completely free model, though Atlas's free tier is also compelling.

Best for Power Users: Atlas's Agent Mode and Claude for Chrome's workflow training offer the most sophisticated automation capabilities.

Best for Privacy-Focused Users: Dia emphasizes privacy in its design philosophy, though all these tools require some level of data access to function.

Best for Existing Ecosystem Integration: Claude for Chrome, as it works within your current browser setup.

Best for Research and Learning: Comet, with its emphasis on cited sources and Perplexity's search capabilities.

The Future of AI Browsing

The AI browser market is projected to explode from $4.5 billion in 2024 to $76.8 billion by 2034. This dramatic growth reflects the fundamental shift in how we'll interact with the web. These four solutions represent different philosophies:

Comet believes AI browsing should be free and search-focused

Atlas envisions autonomous AI agents that work independently

Dia thinks the browser interface itself needs reimagining around AI

Claude for Chrome argues that AI should augment your existing browser rather than replace it

Which Is Right for You?

Choose Comet if: You want a free, full-featured AI browser with strong research capabilities and don't mind Perplexity's advertising-supported model.

Choose Atlas if: You're already in the ChatGPT ecosystem, use macOS, and want cutting-edge agent capabilities (with a paid subscription).

Choose Dia if: You're willing to try a reimagined browser interface and want customizable AI workflows tailored to your specific needs.

Choose Claude for Chrome if: You prefer sticking with Chrome, already use Claude, and want powerful automation without switching browsers.

Final Thoughts

We're witnessing the early days of AI-native browsing, and each of these solutions offers glimpses into different possible futures. The competition is fierce, and that benefits users through rapid innovation and falling prices (witness Comet's shift to free).

Whichever option you choose, one thing is clear: AI is no longer a feature added to browsers—it's becoming the core of how we navigate and interact with the web. The browser wars of 2025 aren't about speed or compatibility; they're about which AI assistant will guide us through the internet.

Need Help Choosing the Right AI Tools for Your Business?

At GLC Web Solutions, we help businesses navigate the rapidly evolving AI landscape. Whether you need guidance on which AI browsing solutions will benefit your team, or you're looking to integrate AI capabilities into your web presence, we're here to help. Get in touch through our contact form to discuss how we can support your digital transformation journey.

item.title: The Biggest Changes to Search in 2025: A Comprehensive Timeline
item.dc:creator: Gareth Cross
item.content:encoded:
2025 has been a landmark year for search technology and SEO strategy. From AI-powered search results to major algorithm updates, the search landscape has transformed significantly. This comprehensive timeline breaks down the biggest changes and what they mean for your digital strategy.

January 2025: AI Integration Takes Center Stage

The new year kicked off with major search engines accelerating their AI integration. Google's enhanced Search Generative Experience (SGE) began rolling out more widely, providing AI-synthesized answers directly in search results for complex queries. This marked a fundamental shift in how users consume search information.

**Key Impact:** SEO strategies needed immediate adjustment as traditional "rank for the keyword" approaches became less effective. Content creators had to focus more on comprehensive, authoritative information that could feed AI summaries.

February 2025: Major Algorithm Update

Google released a significant core update in mid-February that impacted search rankings across most industries. The update focused on rewarding high-quality, original content while penalizing thin, AI-generated content without added value.

**Key Impact:** Websites saw significant ranking fluctuations. Publishers who had invested in genuine expertise and original research maintained strong positions, while those relying on auto-generated content suffered substantial drops.

March 2025: Visual Search Revolution

Major search engines enhanced their visual search capabilities dramatically. The ability to search using images, sketches, and even video clips became mainstream, supported by advanced computer vision and AI models.

**Key Impact:** Image optimization and video metadata became critical SEO components. Businesses had to ensure their visual assets were properly annotated and optimized for AI interpretation.

April-May 2025: E-E-A-T Evolution

Google formally updated its E-E-A-T (Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, Trustworthiness) guidelines, adding new metrics and placing even greater emphasis on verified author credentials and publication date accuracy.

**Key Impact:** Author bios became essential ranking factors. Websites investing in expert-led content and transparent credential verification saw improved rankings in competitive niches.

June 2025: Search Generalist AI Launch

A new generation of AI-powered search competitors began gaining meaningful market share. These specialized search tools offered conversational interfaces and sources directly cited within results, challenging Google's dominance.

**Key Impact:** SEO professionals had to optimize for multiple search platforms, not just Google. Understanding each platform's ranking factors became essential for comprehensive search visibility.

July 2025: Core Web Vitals 2.0

An updated version of Core Web Vitals was introduced with stricter thresholds and new metrics focusing on responsiveness and loading predictability. Mobile performance optimization became even more critical.

**Key Impact:** Websites with poor technical performance experienced ranking drops. Development and engineering teams became more directly involved in SEO strategy decisions.

August 2025: Semantic Search Maturity

Semantic understanding of search intent reached new levels of sophistication. Search engines could understand complex, multi-intent queries and return results that addressed multiple underlying user needs simultaneously.

**Key Impact:** Keyword research methodologies evolved. Focus shifted from exact-match keywords to semantic clusters and answer frameworks that addressed broader user intent patterns.

September 2025: Search Analytics Evolution

New search analytics tools emerged providing deeper insights into AI-generated answer attribution and visual search performance. Traditional click-through data became supplemented with "featured in AI answer" metrics.

**Key Impact:** KPI definitions changed. Success metrics expanded beyond rankings and clicks to include mentions in AI summaries and visual search impressions.

October 2025: Local Search Transformation

Local search results became increasingly AI-personalized, with contextual relevance based on user behavior, preferences, and seasonal facto

item.title: Google Workspace for Business: Complete Guide to Professional Email and Productivity Tools
item.dc:creator: Gareth Cross
item.content:encoded:
In today's digital business landscape, having a professional email address and integrated productivity tools is no longer optional—it's essential. Google Workspace (formerly known as G Suite) offers businesses a comprehensive suite of cloud-based tools that can transform how your team communicates, collaborates, and manages data. In this complete guide, we'll explore the benefits of Google Workspace, break down the costs, walk you through the setup process, and explain how GLC Web Solutions can help you get started.

Google Workspace is Google's professional suite of cloud computing, productivity, and collaboration tools designed for businesses, organizations, and educational institutions. It includes custom email addresses using your own domain (@yourcompany.com), along with access to Google's powerful suite of applications including Gmail, Google Drive, Google Docs, Sheets, Slides, Calendar, Meet, and more—all integrated seamlessly and accessible from anywhere.

Key Benefits of Google Workspace

  1. Professional Email with Your Domain

One of the most significant advantages of Google Workspace is the ability to create professional email addresses using your own domain name (e.g., yourname@yourcompany.co.uk). This immediately boosts your credibility and brand recognition compared to free email services.

  1. Enhanced Collaboration Tools

Google Workspace allows multiple team members to work on the same document simultaneously, with real-time updates and built-in commenting features. No more emailing document versions back and forth—everyone works from a single source of truth.

  1. Generous Storage Space

Depending on your plan, you'll receive between 30GB and unlimited storage per user, shared across Gmail, Google Drive, and Google Photos. This eliminates the need for separate storage solutions.

  1. Advanced Security Features

Google Workspace includes enterprise-grade security with two-factor authentication, advanced phishing and malware protection, data loss prevention, and administrative controls to manage user access and permissions.

  1. Professional Video Conferencing

Google Meet provides high-quality video conferencing for up to 500 participants (on higher plans), with recording capabilities and integration with your calendar.

  1. Mobile Accessibility

Access all your emails, documents, and collaboration tools from any device—desktop, laptop, tablet, or smartphone—with automatic syncing across all platforms.

  1. 99.9% Uptime Guarantee

Google guarantees 99.9% uptime, ensuring your business email and tools are always available when you need them.Google Workspace Pricing Plans (January 2026)

Google Workspace offers several pricing tiers to suit businesses of all sizes. All plans are billed per user, per month:

Business Starter - £4.60 per user/month

  • Custom business email (@yourcompany.com)
  • 30GB storage per user
  • Video conferencing (up to 100 participants)
  • Security and management controls
  • Standard support

Business Standard - £9.20 per user/month

  • Everything in Business Starter
  • 2TB storage per user
  • Video conferencing (up to 150 participants)
  • Recording for video meetings
  • Enhanced security and management controls

Business Plus - £15.50 per user/month

  • Everything in Business Standard
  • 5TB storage per user
  • Video conferencing (up to 500 participants)
  • Enhanced security, including Vault for eDiscovery and retention
  • Advanced endpoint management

Enterprise Plans - Custom pricing

  • Contact Google for enterprise-level solutions with unlimited storage, advanced security features, and premium support.

Note: All plans require an annual commitment for the best pricing, though monthly plans are also available at a slightly higher rate.How to Set Up Google Workspace: Step-by-Step Guide

Setting up Google Workspace involves several technical steps, but the process can be straightforward with proper guidance:

Step 1: Choose Your Plan
Select the Google Workspace plan that best fits your business needs and budget. Consider factors like the number of users, required storage, and desired features.

Step 2: Sign Up and Verify Your Domain
You'll need to verify that you own the domain you want to use with Google Workspace. This typically involves adding a TXT record to your domain's DNS settings.

Step 3: Create User Accounts
Set up email accounts for your team members. You can create multiple users and assign different roles and permissions.

Step 4: Configure MX Records
Update your domain's MX (Mail Exchange) records to point to Google's servers. This ensures that emails sent to your domain are delivered to your Google Workspace inbox.

Step 5: Migrate Existing Email
If you're switching from another email provider, you'll need to migrate your existing emails, contacts, and calendar data to Google Workspace.

Step 6: Set Up Additional Services
Configure Google Drive, Calendar, Meet, and other applications according to your business requirements.

Step 7: Configure Security Settings
Enable two-factor authentication, set up data retention policies, and configure admin console settings to protect your business data.

Step 8: Train Your Team
Ensure all team members understand how to use their new email addresses and Google Workspace tools effectively.How GLC Web Solutions Can Help

While Google Workspace setup might seem complex, you don't have to navigate it alone. At GLC Web Solutions, we specialize in helping UK businesses transition to Google Workspace smoothly and efficiently. Here's how we can assist:

Expert Consultation
We'll assess your business needs and recommend the most appropriate Google Workspace plan for your organization, ensuring you get the features you need without overpaying.

Complete Setup and Configuration
Our team handles all technical aspects of the setup, including:

  • Domain verification
  • DNS record configuration (MX, TXT, CNAME)
  • User account creation
  • Email migration from existing providers
  • Security policy implementation
  • Mobile device setup and management

Seamless Email Migration
We ensure your existing emails, contacts, and calendar appointments are migrated to Google Workspace without any data loss or downtime.

Custom Training
We provide personalized training sessions for your team, ensuring everyone knows how to maximize the productivity tools available in Google Workspace.

Ongoing Support
Our support doesn't end after setup. We offer continued assistance to address any questions or issues that arise as your team adapts to Google Workspace.

Integration Services
We can integrate Google Workspace with your existing business tools and workflows, creating a seamless digital ecosystem for your organization.

Get Started Today

Ready to elevate your business communication and collaboration with Google Workspace? GLC Web Solutions is here to make the transition effortless. Contact us today for a free consultation, and let us handle the technical details while you focus on running your business.

Whether you're a small startup or an established enterprise, professional email and productivity tools are essential for success in 2026. Don't let technical complexity hold you back—let GLC Web Solutions guide you through every step of the process.

Get in touch with us today to discuss your Google Workspace needs and discover how we can help transform your business communications.

item.title: The 20 Biggest New Technology Releases in 2025 and What to Expect in 2026
item.dc:creator: Gareth Cross
item.content:encoded:
As we move deeper into 2026, it's the perfect time to reflect on the game-changing technology releases that dominated 2025 and look ahead at what innovations are reshaping website publishing and digital tools. The past year has been nothing short of transformative, with artificial intelligence continuing to mature, web technologies evolving rapidly, and digital publishing tools becoming more sophisticated.

The 20 Biggest Technology Releases of 2025

1. Claude 4 (Anthropic)

The latest iteration of Claude brought significant improvements in reasoning, code generation, and multimodal capabilities, becoming a go-to tool for developers building AI-powered applications and marketers automating content workflows.

2. OpenAI GPT-5

GPT-5 introduced breakthrough performance in complex reasoning tasks and real-time interaction, making it increasingly viable for customer service automation and sophisticated content generation at scale.

3. Google Gemini 2.0 Advanced Suite

Google expanded its Gemini lineup with specialized models for enterprise, education, and creative professionals, emphasizing integration across Google Workspace and search functionality.

4. Meta's Llama 3.5

Meta's open-source language models became even more accessible to developers and businesses, democratizing AI capabilities for custom applications and reducing dependency on closed-source platforms.

5. Microsoft Copilot Pro for Web

Deep integration of AI into Edge browser, Office 365, and web development tools made Copilot Pro the default assistant for millions of knowledge workers managing digital workflows.

6. Apple Intelligence Framework

Apple introduced on-device AI processing with privacy-first architecture, changing how mobile users interact with web content and bringing real privacy considerations back to the forefront.

7. Next.js 15 & React 19

These frameworks revolutionized client-side rendering with improved server components, AI-native features, and performance optimizations that set new standards for web application development.

8. TypeScript 5.5

The latest TypeScript release introduced advanced type inference and better tooling support, making complex web applications easier to maintain and debug.

9. Vercel's AI SDK 4.0

This toolkit made it significantly easier for developers to integrate large language models into web applications, complete with streaming, token management, and production-ready features.

10. Shopify Hydrogen 2.0

E-commerce sites got a powerful new framework combining commerce, content, and AI to create dynamic storefronts that personalize in real-time.

11. Figma's AI Design Tools

Figma introduced AI-powered design generation, automatic layout suggestions, and design system intelligence, transforming how designers and developers collaborate.

12. Adobe Express with Neural AI

Adobe's suite expanded with neural AI capabilities for automatic design recommendations, content scaling, and instant brand consistency across all digital properties.

13. WordPress 6.6 & Gutenberg Evolution

WordPress continued its evolution as a headless CMS with improved AI content tools, better block patterns, and stronger integration with frontend frameworks.

14. Webflow's AI Website Builder

Webflow launched AI-powered code generation and design suggestions, enabling creators to build sophisticated sites faster without deep technical knowledge.

15. Cloudflare Pages 3.0

Enhanced edge computing capabilities, improved AI inference at the edge, and better SEO optimization tools made Cloudflare Pages a strong alternative to traditional hosting.

16. Supabase Realtime 2.0

This Firebase alternative released major updates to its realtime database and authentication, making it easier to build collaborative, real-time web applications.

17. Cursor IDE 1.0 Release

The AI-first code editor became mainstream, with developers praising its natural language code generation and debugging assistance for web development.

18. Astro 4.0 & Static Site Generation Evolution

Astro introduced hybrid rendering, better island architecture, and improved content collection APIs, appealing to agencies and publishers seeking performance and flexibility.

19. Stripe Apps & Checkout Evolution

Stripe expanded with customizable payment experiences, AI-powered fraud detection, and integration capabilities that strengthened e-commerce security and user experience.

20. Notion AI & Database Expansions

Notion deepened its AI integration with better formula support, database relations, and automation, becoming more powerful for content teams managing complex workflows.

What to Expect in 2026: Website Publishing & Digital Tools

AI Will Be Standard, Not Exceptional: By 2026, AI features won't be novelties—they'll be expected. Website builders, CMS platforms, and design tools will have AI-assisted writing, design, and optimization baked in as default.

Edge Computing Becomes Mainstream: Serverless functions and edge computing will move beyond niche adoption. Expect faster, more responsive websites as computation happens closer to users.

AI-Generated Content Needs Better Governance: As AI content generation tools proliferate, 2026 will bring stricter standards for content attribution, authenticity verification, and disclosure.

Design Tokens & Component Libraries Dominate: The gap between design and development will continue to shrink. Design tokens and automated component libraries will become the standard way teams collaborate.

Real-Time Collaboration Everywhere: Following the success of Google Docs and Figma, expect real-time collaboration to become standard in more tools across the platform.

Search Evolution & AI Overviews Impact: Google's AI Overviews will continue evolving, changing how content appears in search results. Publishers will need strategies to optimize for AI-driven search.

Web Components & Framework Convergence: 2026 will see continued movement toward Web Components as the universal standard. Framework wars will matter less as interoperability improves.

Privacy-First Tools Rise: With Apple Intelligence and increased regulatory scrutiny, expect an entire category of privacy-first publishing and analytics tools.

Content Personalization at Scale: AI-powered personalization will move from luxury to standard. Websites will automatically adapt content, layout, and offers based on visitor context.

Video Becomes Easier to Publish: AI-powered video generation, auto-captioning, and intelligent editing will make video publishing as easy as writing blog posts.

Key Takeaways

The technology landscape of 2026 demands that web professionals stay agile. Start preparing now by auditing your current tech stack, considering how AI might enhance your workflows, and staying informed about emerging standards. The future of web publishing is being written right now, and it's more exciting than ever.

item.title: How to Optimize Your Website for GEO: A Step-by-Step Guide for 2026
item.dc:creator: Gareth Cross
item.content:encoded:
As we move into 2026, the digital landscape is evolving rapidly. While traditional SEO remains important, a new frontier has emerged: Generative Engine Optimization (GEO). With AI-powered search engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, and Claude now answering user queries directly, businesses need to adapt their content strategy to remain visible in this new era.

In this comprehensive guide, we'll walk you through exactly how to optimize your website for GEO and ensure your business gets cited by these AI engines.

What is GEO (Generative Engine Optimization)?

Generative Engine Optimization is the practice of optimizing your content so that AI-powered search engines and chatbots cite your website when answering user queries. Unlike traditional SEO, which focuses on ranking in search result pages, GEO aims to make your content the source that AI engines reference when generating responses.

Recent data shows that AI Overviews now appear in over 13% of all search queries, and this number is expected to continue growing throughout 2026 and beyond.

Step 1: Audit Your Current AI Visibility

Before you begin optimizing, you need to understand where you currently stand. Start by checking if your content is already being cited by AI search engines.

Action Steps:

  • Search for your brand and key topics in ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google's AI Overviews
  • Document which pages are currently being referenced (if any)
  • Identify competitors who are appearing in AI-generated responses
  • Use GEO tracking tools to monitor your AI visibility over time

This baseline audit will help you measure the impact of your optimization efforts.

Step 2: Structure Your Content for Easy Extraction

AI engines favor content that is clearly structured and easy to parse. Pages with clear hierarchies and organized information are 40% more likely to be cited.

Action Steps:

  • Use clear H2 and H3 headings to organize your content
  • Keep paragraphs under 120 words for better readability
  • Create Q&A format sections that match how users ask questions
  • Use bullet points and numbered lists to break down complex information
  • Include an answer table or summary box at the top of key pages with crucial facts and metrics

Example Structure:

  1. Question as heading
  2. Direct answer in 2-3 concise sentences
  3. Supporting information with statistics and examples

Step 3: Implement Strategic Schema Markup

Structured data helps AI systems understand your content's context and relationships. Over 75% of high-performing GEO-optimized pages use schema markup.

Priority Schema Types:

  • Article Schema: Identifies your content as an article with author, publication date, and headline
  • Organization/Person Schema: Establishes authority by identifying your company and content authors
  • FAQ Schema: Perfect for Q&A content that AI engines frequently pull from
  • HowTo Schema: Ideal for step-by-step guides and tutorials

Action Steps:

  • Add JSON-LD structured data to all key pages
  • Validate your schema using Google's Rich Results Test
  • Include visible author information on all content
  • Display last-updated dates prominently and refresh high-value pages quarterly

Step 4: Optimize Technical SEO for AI Crawlers

AI systems rely on efficient crawling, just like traditional search engines. A strong technical foundation is essential for GEO success.

Action Steps:

  • Ensure Mobile Optimization: Make your site responsive and mobile-friendly
  • Improve Page Speed: Compress images, enable browser caching, and use a CDN
  • Use Clean HTML: Avoid hiding critical content behind JavaScript
  • Create an XML Sitemap: Help AI crawlers discover all your important pages
  • Fix Broken Links: Ensure all internal and external links work properly
  • Implement HTTPS: Security is a ranking factor for both SEO and GEO

Your site should load in under 3 seconds on mobile devices for optimal performance.

Step 5: Build E-E-A-T Authority Signals

Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, and Trustworthiness (E-E-A-T) are crucial for AI engines to determine which sources to cite.

Action Steps:

  • Create Detailed Author Bios: Include credentials, experience, and expertise for all content creators
  • Publish Original Research: Create unique data, case studies, and statistics that others will cite
  • Earn Quality Backlinks: Focus on getting mentioned by authoritative industry sites
  • Build Brand Mentions: Get your business featured in relevant publications and directories
  • Display Trust Signals: Add contact information, business address, and customer testimonials
  • Link to Authoritative Sources: Connect to Wikipedia and industry-standard resources

AI engines prefer citing established, credible sources with proven expertise.

Step 6: Write Citation-Friendly Content

Content that AI engines can easily extract and cite needs to be clear, concise, and data-driven.

Action Steps:

  • Use Short, Clear Sentences: Keep key information under 60 characters when possible
  • Include Specific Data: Add statistics, numbers, and metrics that can be cited
  • Write in Active Voice: Make statements direct and authoritative
  • Answer Questions Directly: Place the answer immediately after the question
  • Create Quotable Statements: Craft sentences that stand alone as complete thoughts
  • Avoid Vague Language: Replace "might," "could," and "possibly" with definitive statements

Example: Instead of "Many businesses see improvements," write "Companies implementing GEO see a 40% increase in AI citations within 3 months."

Step 7: Establish Entity Relationships

AI engines understand content better when you clearly define entities and their relationships.

Action Steps:

  • Focus on One Primary Topic: Each page should have one main subject
  • Link to 3-6 Related Entities: Connect your topic to supporting concepts
  • Use Internal Linking: Create a web of related content on your site
  • Reference Authoritative Sources: Link to Wikipedia and industry standards
  • Create Topic Clusters: Build pillar pages with supporting content
  • Use Consistent Terminology: Refer to concepts using the same terms throughout

This helps AI engines understand your expertise and the relationships between topics.

Step 8: Monitor and Measure Your GEO Performance

Tracking your progress is essential to understanding what's working and where to improve.

Key Metrics to Track:

  • AI Citation Rate: How often your content appears in AI-generated responses
  • Brand Mention Frequency: How often AI engines reference your brand
  • Content Visibility Score: Which pages are being cited most frequently
  • Competitor Benchmarking: How your visibility compares to competitors
  • Topic Coverage: Which topics you're being cited for

Recommended Tools:

  • GEO tracking platforms for AI visibility monitoring
  • Google Search Console for traditional SEO metrics
  • Prompt tracking tools to see which queries trigger citations

Set up monthly reviews to assess your progress and adjust your strategy.

Implementing Your GEO Strategy: The Roadmap

Now that you understand the key steps, here's a practical timeline to implement GEO optimization:

Weeks 1-4: Foundation Phase

  • Complete your AI visibility audit
  • Verify technical infrastructure
  • Implement priority schema markup
  • Set up tracking tools

Weeks 5-12: Content Optimization Phase

  • Restructure existing content for extractability
  • Build Q&A format content
  • Establish E-E-A-T authority signals
  • Create original research and data

Weeks 13-20: Growth Phase

  • Map content to customer journey
  • Build entity relationships
  • Earn quality backlinks and mentions
  • Establish continuous optimization cycles

Ongoing: Maintenance

  • Refresh high-value pages quarterly
  • Monitor AI citations monthly
  • Track competitor performance
  • Adapt strategy based on results

Conclusion: The Future is GEO

Generative Engine Optimization represents the next evolution in digital visibility. As AI-powered search engines continue to grow, businesses that optimize for GEO now will have a significant competitive advantage.

The good news is that many GEO best practices align with traditional SEO, so you're not starting from scratch. By implementing the steps outlined in this guide, you'll position your website to be cited by AI engines while maintaining strong traditional search rankings.

Start with the foundation phase, focus on creating structured, authoritative content, and continuously monitor your progress. Remember: GEO is a long-term strategy that requires consistency and adaptation.

Need help implementing GEO for your business? Contact GLC Web Solutions for expert guidance on optimizing your website for the AI-powered future of search.

item.title: ChatGPT Ads: The Complete Guide for UK Advertisers (2026)
item.dc:creator: Gareth Cross
item.content:encoded:
ChatGPT is no longer just a research tool — it is becoming a discovery channel. With OpenAI rolling out advertising to more markets, UK businesses now have a new way to reach people at the moment they ask questions, compare options and decide what to do next.

This guide walks through how ChatGPT ads work in practice: how targeting differs from keyword search, where ads appear, the current limits on age, demographics and UK geography, what you cannot run, how reporting protects privacy, and how to set up tracking and landing pages that convert.

Key GLC Insight:

Now that minimum spend periods have finished across several major platforms, there is a short window for early adopters to steal a competitive advantage over competitors — while also filling the gap left by users who have migrated to AI for their answers.

AI-Powered Ad Targeting: Conceptual Matching

Traditional search ads match keywords. ChatGPT ads move toward conceptual matching — understanding what someone is trying to accomplish from the conversation itself, not just the exact phrase they typed.

Well-targeted placements can connect a question like “how to build a website” with relevant hosting or design offers, while conversational intent from chat history, stated interests and purchase signals can support broader personalisation over time.

For UK advertisers, the opportunity is to align ad copy and landing pages with the questions your customers already ask — before they ever reach Google.

ChatGPT Ad Formats & Placements

ChatGPT separates organic answers from sponsored results. Sponsored units can include a favicon, title, body text and optional image asset — appearing alongside, not inside, the core answer where appropriate.

Think in terms of answer independence: your organic content strategy and your paid placements should complement each other. A user may receive a helpful organic response while still seeing a clearly labelled sponsored option when it is relevant.

Test creative that reads like a natural next step rather than an interruption — especially on mobile, where most ChatGPT sessions happen.

Campaign Limitations & Guardrails

ChatGPT advertising ships with strict guardrails. Campaigns pass through validation, certain subscription tiers may be excluded from ad exposure, and age restrictions apply.

Geographic availability is rolling out market by market. In the UK, delivery is currently country-level only — you cannot yet target a region, city or postcode. The next section covers those targeting limits in full.

Sensitive categories such as health, mental health and politics are prohibited. If your business sits near those lines, plan compliant messaging and landing pages before you spend.

Targeting Limitations: Age, Demographics and UK Geography

Advertisers used to Google Ads and Meta will find ChatGPT’s audience controls thin. You cannot target age ranges, and you do not get age breakdowns in reporting. OpenAI withholds ads from accounts it identifies as under 18, but that is a platform guardrail — not an advertiser control you can set to 25–34 or 55+.

Demographic targeting is not available either. There is no gender, household income, parental status, job title or in-market audience layer. You cannot get granular in the way a Google or Meta campaign can. The main lever you control is context hints at ad-group level — descriptions of the conversations you want to appear in — plus country at campaign level. Relevance comes from the chat, not from slicing an audience.

For UK advertisers, geography is currently country-only. You can choose the United Kingdom; you cannot target London, the South-East, a city, a postcode or a radius. Finer location targeting has appeared in some other markets, but it is not available here yet. Local service businesses should treat ChatGPT ads as a national discovery channel and qualify location on the landing page and in the conversation, rather than expecting a geo-fence.

Data & Analytics

Reporting is built around aggregate metrics, not personal identifiers. Names, emails and other PII are blocked before performance data is surfaced — you see impressions, clicks and CTR at campaign level.

Context hints such as location, device and time of day can still inform delivery without exposing individual users. UTM parameters flow through to your web analytics so ChatGPT can sit inside a broader measurement stack.

Pair platform reporting with Google Analytics or your preferred attribution tool so you can compare ChatGPT performance against search, social and other channels.

Budget & Cost Controls

One of the most significant shifts for early testers is the removal of heavy minimum spend requirements on some platforms — lowering the barrier to experiment while auctions mature.

Bidding follows a second-price auction model: if you bid £20 and the next highest bid is £15, you pay £15. Daily budgets can flex up to roughly 2× on high-opportunity days while weekly caps prevent runaway spend.

Start with controlled test budgets, measure incrementally, and scale only when landing page conversion data supports it.

Setting Up Conversion Tracking

Reliable tracking starts with a base pixel snippet placed in your site’s <head> section, then event definitions for the actions that matter — add to cart, lead form submit, purchase and so on.

Use the platform’s test console to verify events before scaling spend. Map the full funnel from awareness through consideration to conversion so you know which placements and messages move revenue, not just clicks.

If you already run Meta or Google tags, treat ChatGPT as another source in the same measurement framework rather than a standalone silo.

Bespoke Landing Page Optimization

ChatGPT traffic arrives with conversational context. Your landing page should continue the dialogue — matching headline, ad copy and on-page H1 so the visitor never feels dropped into a generic homepage.

Use UTM parameters to personalise greetings or offers where appropriate, keep primary CTAs above the fold on mobile, and prioritise load speed. A fast, frictionless page is especially important when users compare you to AI-generated answers in the same session.

Asset synergy between ad and page is not optional here; it is the difference between a curious click and a qualified lead.

Ready to test ChatGPT ads in the UK?

The window for early adoption is real — but it will not stay open forever. If you want help scoping a test campaign, landing page and tracking setup, GLC Web Solutions can map a practical first step without unnecessary spend.

Contact Gareth at GLC Web Solutions to discuss ChatGPT ads, paid media and landing page support for your business.
